review_text: When I signed up, until I uploaded all the documents they kept reading me about it and once I uploaded they didn’t bother to do any KYC. When I decided to checkout the app with a small amount, they waited until I transferred the money and then told me my ePAN cannot be accepted for KYC and kept my order pending. Note the NAV was around INR 27. Despite explaining on 2 calls they wouldn’t respect IT department directive that ePAN is equally valid. So I told them to refund the money, they replied we have initiated the refund and it will come back to account in 3 working days. Simultaneously another of their executive kept emailing me several times for me to email him the PAN scan. I didn’t bother to reply as my refund was in progress as per the Team Lead who spoke last. Separately 2 days later I found the PAN scan and uploaded it in the app. Now suddenly on Monday 3 days after my request for refund, I receive a note saying the money has been sent to the Mutual Fund and units will be allocated in 3 or 4 days. Finally the next day I receive a note saying I have been allocated x units @ NAV INR 29. Not only I had lost INR 2 per unit because of Groww’s mistakes and delays but also the cancellation that was initiated did not happen or they plainly lied to a customer. If this is how investors have to suffer at the hands of new age Brokers like Groww, I would rather desist from investing through such cheap apps. It’s funny their slogan is “proudly built in India for India.” They are apparently in business from 2016. Maybe that’s their level of professionalism. But they should drag the country’s reputation along with it. I humbly request them to change their slogan.

title: Disappointing Trading Experience with the Groww App
review_text: I have been using the Groww app for my trading activities for some time now, and unfortunately, my experience has been far from satisfactory. The app's regular lagging during trading sessions is incredibly frustrating and has cost me valuable opportunities. It's quite disheartening to see such a fundamental flaw persisting in the app despite repeated updates. One of the most crucial features for any trading app is a reliable stop-loss mechanism. Regrettably, Groww's stop-loss functionality is far from dependable. There have been numerous instances where the stop-loss orders were not executed properly, causing significant losses on my trades. It's alarming to see stop-loss orders being executed at 5% loss, only to refresh the app and find it has ballooned to 15% or even 20%. Such discrepancies are simply unacceptable and have shaken my trust in the app. Moreover, the lack of prompt customer support from Groww adds to the frustration. When I encountered issues with the app, reaching out for assistance proved to be an arduous process, and the responses were often generic and unhelpful. The app's user interface is visually appealing and offers a wide variety of investment options, but all of these features become meaningless if the basic functionality of the app is severely flawed. As a result of these consistent issues, I can't help but consider Groww as one of the worst trading apps I've ever used. Trading is a fast-paced activity, and such lags and glitches can have severe financial consequences for users. I genuinely hope that Groww addresses these issues promptly and diligently, as it has the potential to be a great platform if it can deliver a seamless and reliable trading experience. In its current state, I cannot recommend the Groww app for trading purposes. It's vital to have confidence in the platform you use for investing, and unfortunately, the app's persistent lagging and unreliable stop-loss functionality have robbed me of that trust. Until substantial improvements are made, I will be exploring other options for my trading needs

review_text: I’ve been using the Groww App for mutual fund investments, but I’m quite disappointed with a major concern that hasn’t been addressed. Groww is directly storing mutual fund units in DEMAT format without taking proper consent or providing clear choice to investors regarding their preferred holding format — whether DEMAT or SOA (Statement of Account). Many investors prefer SOA format as it gives more flexibility (especially for switching platforms or offline transactions) and avoids unnecessary DP charges. However, Groww doesn’t offer an option to choose and automatically links all investments to the DEMAT account held with them. This is not just a matter of user experience, but an important investment decision, and Groww must take explicit consent from the investor before choosing the holding format. For a platform that claims to be investor-friendly, this is quite disappointing. I hope Groww takes this feedback seriously and starts providing the option to select the holding mode during mutual fund investment – the way other platforms like Sharekhan or MF Central do.

For example: - If I want to invest ₹10 lakh or more in one go during market correction, it is not possible smoothly using mandate - I have to split transactions or use manual payment, which defeats the purpose of AutoPay Other platforms like NJ Wealth provide higher mandate flexibility (₹20–50 lakh or more), which is much more practical for high-value investors. 👉 Request: Please introduce higher mandate limits (₹20–50 lakh or customizable based on user profile and bank approval), especially via net banking/eMandate. --- 2) Limited SIP Frequency Options Currently, SIP options are limited to monthly (and some dates). 👉 Missing features: - Daily SIP option - Weekly SIP option These are very useful for: - Better cost averaging - Investing during volatile markets - More flexible cash flow management Many investors prefer daily/weekly SIP to capture market movements more effectively. --- ✅ Overall: Groww is a very user-friendly and excellent platform, but these limitations make it less suitable for high-value and advanced investors. Improving mandate limits and adding flexible SIP frequencies will significantly enhance the platform experience.

This is a good option for global diversification considering investment through mutual fund route is almost closed since early 2022. Also, dividends of UCITS are reinvested automatically inside the Fund. Platforms such as IndMoney do offer UCITS ETF. Since Groww is a very progressive organisation and takes pride in always keeping its ears to the ground and giving customer satisfaction highest importance, I hope Groww team takes note of this suggestion.
